Build a test report step by step

Source: R/test-report.R
report_start.Rd

Start a report with report_start(), then add the parts you want, in the order you want them, and write it with report_save(). Printing a report previews it in the viewer. test_report() builds the default report in one call.

Usage

report_start(x, lt1 = NULL, lt2 = NULL, dates = NULL)

report_header(report, name = NULL, date = NULL, ..., lab = NULL, logo = NULL)

report_summary(report)

report_zones(report, model = 5, chart = TRUE)

report_progress(report, cv = NULL)

report_reference(report)

report_prediction(report)

report_checks(report)

report_test(report, protocol = NULL)

report_methods(report)

report_text(report, title, text)

report_page_break(report)

report_save(
  report,
  file = "lactate-test-report.html",
  pdf = FALSE,
  open = interactive()
)

Arguments

x

The result of lactate_threshold(), or a list of two to five of them for a series of tests of one athlete.

lt1, lt2

The thresholds that mark LT1 and LT2, as in lactate_zones().

dates

For a series, the date of each test: dates, or days since the first test. Without them, the names of x are read as dates.

report

A report from report_start().

name

The athlete's name, the heading of the report.

date

The date of the test, as you want it printed.

...

Other details to list under the name, as label = value, e.g. sex = "female", age = 27, club = "Tuebingen RC". body_mass (kg, a number) also gives the thresholds per kg.

lab

Your lab, institution or business, printed at the top.

logo

The path to a logo image (PNG or JPEG), printed at the top right.

model

3 or 5 zones.

chart

Whether to draw the zones chart above the table.

cv

The typical error of the methods, as in compare_tests(); the defaults cover only some methods.

protocol

One line on how the test was done: ergometer, stages, sampling site, analyzer.

title

The heading of a section of your own.

text

Its text: one string per paragraph.

file

Where to write the report, an .html file.

pdf

Whether to print a PDF next to the HTML file as well. Needs the pagedown package and Google Chrome or Chromium.

open

Whether to open the report in the browser.

Value

a lactate_test_report to add to, and for report_save() the path of the report, invisibly.

Details

To report a series of tests of one athlete, give report_start() a list of tests and their dates: the sections above then describe the latest test, and report_progress() shows the progress over all of them.

  • report_header(): who was tested and where. The athlete's name, the date, any other details you name (sex, age, club, tester...), your lab or institution, and its logo.

  • report_summary(): the answer: what LT1 and LT2 mean, and LT1, LT2 and the peak with their lactate, heart rate, RPE, percentage of peak and, with body_mass, per kg.

  • report_progress(): for a series, how LT1 and LT2 changed since the first test, every lactate curve with the zones of each test, test by test, and whether the latest change is larger than the noise of the method (compare_tests()).

  • report_zones(): the zones chart and table, three or five zones.

  • report_reference(): for cycling, the percentile of the power at 3 mmol/L and at baseline + 1 mmol/L among people of the same age and sex in Germany (reference_percentiles()), from the age, sex and body_mass given to report_header(). For the general population, not for athletes.

  • report_prediction(): the predicted race performance, from the chosen thresholds when an equation takes them.

  • report_checks(): what to double-check in the data.

  • report_test(): the protocol and the measured stages.

  • report_methods(): the threshold of every method.

  • report_text(): a section of your own, such as notes or a training plan.

  • report_page_break(): start a new page when printed.

Examples

results <- lactate_threshold(
  demo_data, intensity, lactate, heart_rate, rpe_column = rpe, plot = FALSE
)
report <- report_start(results) |>
  report_header(
    name = "Demo athlete", date = "3 November 2026", sex = "male", age = 31, body_mass = 72,
    lab = "Exercise physiology lab"
  ) |>
  report_summary() |>
  report_zones(model = 3) |>
  report_text("Training", "Two sessions a week in zone 2, one in zone 3.")
report_save(report, tempfile(fileext = ".html"), open = FALSE)
